// Prints a Benchmark Mode run (scripts/bench.sh) as one table per scenario, next to a baseline run when there is one.

// null where the platform has no per-thread CPU time (Vita3K).
cpu: { ui_pct: number; js_pct: number | null } | null;
type Result = { platform: string; clock_overhead_ns: number; measure_s: number; scenarios: Scenario[] };
type Meta = { target: string; commit: string; dirty: boolean; date: string; machine: string };
type Run = { result: Result; meta: Meta | null };
// Lower is better unless noted. A change smaller than noise, in the metric's unit, is not called better or worse.
{ label: "UI work p50 ms", value: (s) => s.frames.work?.p50 },
{ label: "UI work p95 ms", value: (s) => s.frames.work?.p95 },

{ label: "Input handler p95 ms", value: (s) => s.js?.input_handler?.p95 },

return a === undefined || b === undefined ? undefined : a + b;
async function readJson<T>(file: string): Promise<T | null> {
return existsSync(file) ? (JSON.parse(await readFile(file, "utf8")) as T) : null;
async function readRun(dir: string): Promise<Run | null> {
return result && { result, meta: await readJson<Meta>(path.join(dir, "meta.json")) };
function delta(metric: Metric, value: number | undefined, base: number | undefined): string {
// Back-to-back Vita3K runs differ by up to about 10%, and by tens of microseconds on sub-millisecond spans.
return `${where} (${run.result.measure_s} s per scenario, clock read ${run.result.clock_overhead_ns} ns)`;
const widths = rows[0]?.map((_, column) => Math.max(...rows.map((row) => row[column]?.length ?? 0))) ?? [];
const baseline = baselineDir ? await readRun(baselineDir) : null;
console.log("Warning: the baseline ran on another machine, so emulator and host numbers do not compare.");

description: Measures VitaDeck performance with Benchmark Mode on the Vita, in Vita3K, or on the desktop host, and compares a run against the committed baseline. Use when the user asks about performance, CPU use, frame time, FPS, slow rendering or slow React updates, wants a benchmark or baseline, or wants to check whether a change made VitaDeck faster or slower.

`scripts/bench.sh` runs VitaDeck in Benchmark Mode ([ADR 0005](../../../docs/adr/0005-benchmark-mode-in-the-shipping-binary.md)), then prints each scenario next to the baseline in `tests/bench/baselines/<target>/`:
scripts/bench.sh vita3k                       # build the VPK, run every scenario in Vita3K
scripts/bench.sh vita                         # same on the Vita at $PSVITAIP
scripts/bench.sh host minesweeper-navigate    # one scenario on the desktop host
scripts/bench.sh vita3k --no-build            # rerun the existing build
Results land in `out-bench/<target>-<time>/` (`result.json`, `meta.json`, `log.txt`). `pnpm --dir js bench:report <run dir> [baseline dir]` reprints any run against any other.

- `vita` is the source of truth. Ask Máté before running it; it is his device. It needs VitaShell's FTP server (1337) and vitacompanion (1338) running, uploads `eboot.bin`, `runtime.js`, the example Deck Apps, and any fonts or emoji the Vita lacks (the first time, about 4000 emoji take most of an hour), and leaves the Vita on the LiveArea when done. Get the IP from Máté rather than scanning for it: a bare connection such as `nc -z` crashes VitaShell's FTP and vitacompanion until the Vita restarts.

- `vita3k` needs the emulator set up (`vitadeck-emulator` skill). Its numbers depend on the machine running it, so compare only against a baseline recorded on the same machine (`meta.json` says which).
- `host` is fast for checking that a scenario works, but says little about the Vita.
1. Record a baseline on the target you care about, from `main`: `scripts/bench.sh vita3k --update-baseline`.

2. Make the change, then run `scripts/bench.sh vita3k` and read the change column. The report only calls a change better or worse past 10%, about the run-to-run spread in Vita3K; rerun once before trusting a small win.
3. When a PR changes performance, put the report in the PR body and commit the new baseline with it.

Each one starts with a Deck App Runtime Restart, plays its setup script, warms up for 3 s, then measures for 10 s while its loop script plays. They live in `SCENARIOS` in `src/core/bench.c`; add one there, scripted against an example Deck App, and re-record the baselines.
| `minesweeper-idle` | Steady drawing of a dense static screen (145 Buttons) |
| `minesweeper-navigate` | React re-render and commit on every D-pad move (10 per second) |
| `demo-text` | Wrapped Latin, CJK and emoji text |
| `demo-scroll` | Native scrolling of a 40-row Scroll under the left stick, no React work |

- **UI work** is the UI thread's CPU-side frame cost: `input`, `layout` (the render lock, plus layout on frames with a new snapshot), `glyphs`, `draw`, `shell`. **Begin + present** is `BeginDrawing` and `EndDrawing`: GPU sync, buffer swap, vsync and the frame limiter, mostly waiting, and the wait moves between the two from run to run. The frame budget is 16.7 ms.

- **UI/JS thread CPU %** is CPU time the OS charged to each thread over the window, idle polling included. On the Vita it comes from `runClocks`; Vita3K does not implement that, so it shows `-` there.

- **Input latency** is from an input event entering the queue to its JS handler returning, synchronous React render included. When it climbs far past the busy iteration time, the Deck App is not keeping up and events are queuing.

- **JS busy ms/s** is time the JS thread spent outside its idle sleep: input handlers, timers, fetch callbacks, microtasks and snapshot swaps, plus about 250 empty polls a second when idle (a millisecond or two per second in Vita3K). React renders inside these. **Commit** is React's commit phase alone (`prepareForCommit` to `resetAfterCommit`), so busy time minus commit time is mostly React rendering.
- **Native mutations** counts the reconciler's calls into C. Many commits with zero mutations means React re-rendered without changing anything on screen.
- **Startup** is the JS thread from creation to the first published snapshot: `runtime.js`, the Deck App Package Entry and the first render.
- `src/core/` - bootstrap, QuickJS runtime, event queue, package library and manifest parsing (vendored `vendor/jimp/jimp.h`, see ADR 0003)
- `src/core/` - bootstrap, QuickJS runtime, event queue, package library and manifest parsing (vendored `vendor/jimp/jimp.h`, see ADR 0003), Benchmark Mode (`bench.c`, see ADR 0005)
- `src/jslib/` - native functions exposed to JS: instances, timers, fetch, log, colors
- `src/ui/` - instance tree, rendering, fonts, images, input, scroll
- `src/shell/` - VitaDeck Shell; `src/upload/` - Runtime Upload listener; `src/platform/` - threads (POSIX vs Vita)
- `js/packages/sdk/` - `@vitadeck/sdk`: author-facing components, theme, types, and the `vitadeck` CLI (`cli/`, scaffold under `cli/templates/`)
- `js/packages/runtime/` - the React reconciler bundle the host embeds
- `js/examples/` - example Deck Apps; the smoke test screenshots every section of `demo`

- `tests/` - CTest harnesses (`smoke_harness.c`, `package_manifest_harness.c`, `package_library_harness.c`, `timer_reload_harness.c`, `upload_parsing_harness.c`), golden screenshots (`fixtures/golden/`), and benchmark baselines (`bench/baselines/`)
- `vendor/quickjs` - git submodule; `docker-compose.yml` + `Dockerfile` - Vitasdk and Linux smoke images

- `.agents/skills/` - repo skills (`vitadeck-build`, `vitadeck-emulator`, `vitadeck-smoke`, `vitadeck-manual-testing`, `vitadeck-vdapp-upload`, `vitadeck-deck-app-init`) plus `comprehende` installed from `matemolnar8/comprehende` via the `skills` CLI (`skills-lock.json`) and `pages`, a repo-owned skill with its own publish script. `.claude/skills` symlinks here. - Write React for the React Compiler: pure renders, Rules of Hooks, accurate effect deps, no manual `useMemo`/`useCallback`/`memo`.

diff --git a/scripts/bench.sh b/scripts/bench.sh
new file mode 100755
index 0000000..ef3dfd5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/bench.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,209 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+ROOT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+TITLE_ID="PGRI00001"
+VITA3K_HOME="${VITADECK_VITA3K_HOME:-$HOME/.vitadeck/vita3k}"
+RESULT_TIMEOUT_S="${VITADECK_BENCH_TIMEOUT:-300}"
+
+usage() {
+  cat <<'EOF'
+usage: scripts/bench.sh <host|vita3k|vita> [--no-build] [--update-baseline] [scenario...]
+
+Runs VitaDeck in Benchmark Mode (src/core/bench.c) and prints a report against tests/bench/baselines/<target>.
+Without scenarios it runs all of them. Results go to out-bench/<target>-<time>/.
+
+host     The desktop build in out/.
+vita3k   The VPK in the Vita3K emulator (see the vitadeck-emulator skill).
+vita     The VPK on the Vita at $PSVITAIP, through VitaShell's FTP (1337) and vitacompanion (1338).
+
+--no-build          Run the existing build.
+--update-baseline   Also copy the results to tests/bench/baselines/<target>; needs every scenario to run and pass.
+
+Environment:
+  PSVITAIP                 Vita IP, for vita
+  VITADECK_VITA3K_HOME     Emulator config and storage (default: ~/.vitadeck/vita3k)
+  VITADECK_BENCH_TIMEOUT   Seconds to wait for the result (default: 300)
+EOF
+}
+
+step() {
+  printf '\n==> %s\n' "$1"
+}
+
+die() {
+  printf '%s\n' "$1" >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+
+TARGET="${1:-}"
+[[ "$TARGET" == "host" || "$TARGET" == "vita3k" || "$TARGET" == "vita" ]] || {
+  usage >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+shift
+BUILD=1
+UPDATE_BASELINE=0
+SCENARIOS=()
+for arg in "$@"; do
+  case "$arg" in
+    --no-build) BUILD=0 ;;
+    --update-baseline) UPDATE_BASELINE=1 ;;
+    -h | --help)
+      usage
+      exit 0
+      ;;
+    -*) die "Unknown option $arg" ;;
+    *) SCENARIOS+=("$arg") ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+# A baseline holds every scenario, so it is only replaced by a full run.
+((UPDATE_BASELINE == 0 || ${#SCENARIOS[@]} == 0)) || die "--update-baseline needs a run of every scenario."
+
+RUN_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/out-bench/$TARGET-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
+mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR"
+REQUEST="${SCENARIOS[*]:-}"
+
+wait_for() {
+  local description="$1"
+  shift
+  local deadline=$((SECONDS + RESULT_TIMEOUT_S))
+  until "$@"; do
+    ((SECONDS < deadline)) || die "Timed out waiting for $description."
+    sleep 2
+  done
+}
+
+build_js() {
+  step "Build JS"
+  pnpm --dir "$ROOT_DIR/js" build
+}
+
+build_vpk() {
+  build_js
+  step "Build VPK"
+  (cd "$ROOT_DIR" && docker compose run --rm -T vitasdk bash -lc "cmake -S . -B out-vita && cmake --build out-vita")
+}
+
+run_host() {
+  if ((BUILD)); then
+    build_js
+    step "Build host"
+    cmake -S "$ROOT_DIR" -B "$ROOT_DIR/out" >/dev/null
+    cmake --build "$ROOT_DIR/out" --target vitadeck stage_examples
+  fi
+  local data="$ROOT_DIR/out/vitadeck-data"
+  mkdir -p "$data/bench"
+  rm -f "$data/bench/result.json"
+  printf '%s\n' "$REQUEST" >"$data/bench/request"
+  step "Benchmark (host)"
+  (cd "$ROOT_DIR/out" && VITADECK_DATA_ROOT="$data" ./vitadeck) >"$RUN_DIR/log.txt" 2>&1 ||
+    die "vitadeck failed; see $RUN_DIR/log.txt"
+  [[ -f "$data/bench/result.json" ]] || die "No result; see $RUN_DIR/log.txt"
+  cp "$data/bench/result.json" "$RUN_DIR/result.json"
+}
+
+run_vita3k() {
+  if ((BUILD)); then build_vpk; fi
+  local data="$VITA3K_HOME/fs/ux0/data/vitadeck"
+  mkdir -p "$data/bench"
+  rm -f "$data/bench/result.json"
+  printf '%s\n' "$REQUEST" >"$data/bench/request"
+  step "Benchmark (Vita3K, quits with the app)"
+  "$ROOT_DIR/scripts/vita3k.sh" launch >"$RUN_DIR/log.txt" 2>&1 || true
+  [[ -f "$data/bench/result.json" ]] || die "No result; see $RUN_DIR/log.txt"
+  cp "$data/bench/result.json" "$RUN_DIR/result.json"
+}
+
+vita_exists() {
+  curl -sf --max-time 10 -o /dev/null "ftp://$PSVITAIP:1337/ux0:/data/vitadeck/bench/$1"
+}
+
+# Only a missing file (curl 78) counts; a timeout while the app starts does not.
+vita_request_consumed() {
+  local status=0
+  vita_exists request || status=$?
+  ((status == 78))
+}
+
+vita_result_written() {
+  vita_exists result.json
+}
+
+# Prints curl config lines uploading the files in a local asset directory that the Vita lacks. The assets are pinned
+# downloads, so a name already on the Vita is the same file. VitaShell's FTP has no NLST, so this parses LIST. The first
+# run uploads about 4000 emoji, which takes most of an hour as VitaShell slows down with the directory's size.
+missing_asset_uploads() {
+  local dir="$ROOT_DIR/assets/$1" remote="ftp://$PSVITAIP:1337/ux0:/app/$TITLE_ID/assets/$1"
+  [[ -d "$dir" ]] || return 0
+  comm -23 <(ls "$dir" | sort) <(curl -s --max-time 60 "$remote/" | tr -d '\r' | awk '{ print $NF }' | sort) |
+    while read -r name; do
+      printf 'upload-file = "%s"\nurl = "%s/%s"\n' "$dir/$name" "$remote" "$name"
+    done
+}
+
+run_vita() {
+  [[ -n "${PSVITAIP:-}" ]] || die "Set PSVITAIP to the Vita's IP."
+  if ((BUILD)); then build_vpk; fi
+  local ftp="ftp://$PSVITAIP:1337/ux0:"
+  local stage
+  stage=$(mktemp -d)
+  trap 'rm -rf "$stage"' RETURN
+
+  step "Upload VitaDeck, its fonts and emoji, and the example Deck Apps"
+  echo destroy | nc "$PSVITAIP" 1338 || true
+  curl -sS -T "$ROOT_DIR/out-vita/eboot.bin" "$ftp/app/$TITLE_ID/"
+  curl -sS -T "$ROOT_DIR/js/dist/runtime/runtime.js" "$ftp/app/$TITLE_ID/js/runtime.js"
+  "$ROOT_DIR/scripts/stage-example-apps.sh" "$ROOT_DIR" "$stage" >/dev/null
+  (
+    cd "$stage"
+    printf 'ftp-create-dirs\nsilent\nshow-error\n'
+    find installed-deck-apps -type f | while read -r file; do
+      printf 'upload-file = "%s"\nurl = "%s/data/vitadeck/%s"\n' "$stage/$file" "$ftp" "$file"
+    done
+    missing_asset_uploads fonts
+    missing_asset_uploads emoji
+  ) >"$stage/upload.curl"
+  curl -K "$stage/upload.curl"
+
+  step "Benchmark (Vita)"
+  curl -s -o /dev/null -Q "-DELE result.json" "$ftp/data/vitadeck/bench/" || true
+  printf '%s\n' "$REQUEST" | curl -sS --ftp-create-dirs -T - "$ftp/data/vitadeck/bench/request"
+  echo launch "$TITLE_ID" | nc "$PSVITAIP" 1338
+  wait_for "VitaDeck to start Benchmark Mode" vita_request_consumed
+  wait_for "the result" vita_result_written
+  curl -sS -o "$RUN_DIR/result.json" "$ftp/data/vitadeck/bench/result.json"
+}
+
+"run_$TARGET"
+
+machine() {
+  if [[ "$TARGET" == "vita" ]]; then
+    echo "PS Vita"
+  else
+    echo "$(uname -sm) $( (sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string 2>/dev/null || grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f2) | sed 's/^ *//')"
+  fi
+}
+
+cat >"$RUN_DIR/meta.json" <<EOF
+{
+  "target": "$TARGET",
+  "commit": "$(git -C "$ROOT_DIR" rev-parse --short HEAD)",
+  "dirty": $([[ -n "$(git -C "$ROOT_DIR" status --porcelain -- src js/packages js/examples CMakeLists.txt)" ]] && echo true || echo false),
+  "date": "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)",
+  "machine": "$(machine)"
+}
+EOF
+
+BASELINE="$ROOT_DIR/tests/bench/baselines/$TARGET"
+step "Report"
+pnpm --dir "$ROOT_DIR/js" --silent bench:report "$RUN_DIR" "$BASELINE" | tee "$RUN_DIR/report.txt"
+echo "Results: $RUN_DIR"
+
+if ((UPDATE_BASELINE)); then
+  ! grep -q '"error"' "$RUN_DIR/result.json" || die "A scenario failed, so $BASELINE is unchanged."
+  mkdir -p "$BASELINE"
+  cp "$RUN_DIR/result.json" "$RUN_DIR/meta.json" "$BASELINE/"
+  echo "Updated $BASELINE"
+fi

index 0000000..3a6c209
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.agents/skills/vitadeck-bench/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+---
+name: vitadeck-bench
+description: Measures VitaDeck performance with Benchmark Mode on the Vita, in Vita3K, or on the desktop host, and compares a run against the committed baseline. Use when the user asks about performance, CPU use, frame time, FPS, slow rendering or slow React updates, wants a benchmark or baseline, or wants to check whether a change made VitaDeck faster or slower.
+metadata:
+  internal: true
+---
+
+# VitaDeck benchmarks
+
+`scripts/bench.sh` runs VitaDeck in Benchmark Mode ([ADR 0005](../../../docs/adr/0005-benchmark-mode-in-the-shipping-binary.md)), then prints each scenario next to the baseline in `tests/bench/baselines/<target>/`:
+
+```sh
+scripts/bench.sh vita3k                       # build the VPK, run every scenario in Vita3K
+scripts/bench.sh vita                         # same on the Vita at $PSVITAIP
+scripts/bench.sh host minesweeper-navigate    # one scenario on the desktop host
+scripts/bench.sh vita3k --no-build            # rerun the existing build
+```
+
+Results land in `out-bench/<target>-<time>/` (`result.json`, `meta.json`, `log.txt`). `pnpm --dir js bench:report <run dir> [baseline dir]` reprints any run against any other.
+
+- `vita` is the source of truth. Ask Máté before running it; it is his device. It needs VitaShell's FTP server (1337) and vitacompanion (1338) running, uploads `eboot.bin`, `runtime.js`, the example Deck Apps, and any fonts or emoji the Vita lacks (the first time, about 4000 emoji take most of an hour), and leaves the Vita on the LiveArea when done. Get the IP from Máté rather than scanning for it: a bare connection such as `nc -z` crashes VitaShell's FTP and vitacompanion until the Vita restarts.
+- `vita3k` needs the emulator set up (`vitadeck-emulator` skill). Its numbers depend on the machine running it, so compare only against a baseline recorded on the same machine (`meta.json` says which).
+- `host` is fast for checking that a scenario works, but says little about the Vita.
+
+## The loop
+
+1. Record a baseline on the target you care about, from `main`: `scripts/bench.sh vita3k --update-baseline`.
+2. Make the change, then run `scripts/bench.sh vita3k` and read the change column. The report only calls a change better or worse past 10%, about the run-to-run spread in Vita3K; rerun once before trusting a small win.
+3. When a PR changes performance, put the report in the PR body and commit the new baseline with it.
+
+## Scenarios
+
+Each one starts with a Deck App Runtime Restart, plays its setup script, warms up for 3 s, then measures for 10 s while its loop script plays. They live in `SCENARIOS` in `src/core/bench.c`; add one there, scripted against an example Deck App, and re-record the baselines.
+
+| Scenario | What it stresses |
+|---|---|
+| `minesweeper-idle` | Steady drawing of a dense static screen (145 Buttons) |
+| `minesweeper-navigate` | React re-render and commit on every D-pad move (10 per second) |
+| `demo-text` | Wrapped Latin, CJK and emoji text |
+| `demo-scroll` | Native scrolling of a 40-row Scroll under the left stick, no React work |
+
+## Reading the numbers
+
+- **UI work** is the UI thread's CPU-side frame cost: `input`, `layout` (the render lock, plus layout on frames with a new snapshot), `glyphs`, `draw`, `shell`. **Begin + present** is `BeginDrawing` and `EndDrawing`: GPU sync, buffer swap, vsync and the frame limiter, mostly waiting, and the wait moves between the two from run to run. The frame budget is 16.7 ms.
+- **UI/JS thread CPU %** is CPU time the OS charged to each thread over the window, idle polling included. On the Vita it comes from `runClocks`; Vita3K does not implement that, so it shows `-` there.
+- **Input latency** is from an input event entering the queue to its JS handler returning, synchronous React render included. When it climbs far past the busy iteration time, the Deck App is not keeping up and events are queuing.
+- **JS busy ms/s** is time the JS thread spent outside its idle sleep: input handlers, timers, fetch callbacks, microtasks and snapshot swaps, plus about 250 empty polls a second when idle (a millisecond or two per second in Vita3K). React renders inside these. **Commit** is React's commit phase alone (`prepareForCommit` to `resetAfterCommit`), so busy time minus commit time is mostly React rendering.
+- **Native mutations** counts the reconciler's calls into C. Many commits with zero mutations means React re-rendered without changing anything on screen.
+- **Startup** is the JS thread from creation to the first published snapshot: `runtime.js`, the Deck App Package Entry and the first render.
